recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆受感染的紅血球內有形狀不規則、伸展成變形蟲狀（ameboid）的藍色滋養體，並帶有棕色瘧色素顆粒，受感染紅血球有輕度增大；這種變形蟲樣滋養體符合間日瘧原蟲（Plasmodium vivax）。
features: Single infected red cell with an irregular, ameboid blue-staining trophozoite
Fine brownish malarial pigment (hemozoin) within the parasite
Parasite occupies a large portion of the red cell, with the host cell mildly enlarged and pale
Schüffner stippling not clearly resolved at this focus
Background of thick-area, overlapping uninfected red cells and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single infected red cell containing an irregular, ameboid trophozoite with blue cytoplasm and fine brown hemozoin pigment, occupying much of a mildly enlarged host cell. Schüffner stippling is not clearly resolved in this thick area of the smear. The remaining red cells are uninfected. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection; species confirmation on a thin film (enlarged red cells, Schüffner dots, all stages present) or by antigen/PCR testing and parasitemia quantification are recommended.

ddx.vs: P. ovale trophozoites are more compact within oval, fimbriated enlarged red cells, whereas P. vivax trophozoites are ameboid.
P. falciparum shows small delicate ring forms, often multiple per normal-sized red cell with appliqué forms and banana-shaped gametocytes, without enlarged host cells.
P. malariae shows compact band-form trophozoites in normal-sized or small red cells with coarse pigment.
An overlying platelet has granular purple content without a chromatin dot, blue parasite cytoplasm, or pigment, and a halo in the same focal plane.
